title: The Best of Manners
body: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: 'The best among you are those who have the best manners and character.' A reminder that how we treat others each morning shapes the kind of day — and life — we build.

questions.question: What quality does the passage say is most important?
questions.explanation: Good manners and character are highlighted as the best qualities.

title: Seeking Knowledge
body: Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim. The first word revealed in the Quran was 'Iqra' (Read). Starting your day by learning something new brings you closer to your purpose.

questions.question: What was the first word revealed in the Quran?
questions.explanation: The first revealed word was 'Iqra', which means Read.

title: Power of Gratitude
body: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]. True gratitude isn't just saying 'Alhamdulillah', it is using the blessings you have been given in ways that please the Creator.

questions.question: What happens when you are grateful?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that gratitude leads to an increase in favor.

title: Control of Anger
body: The strong man is not the good wrestler; the strong man is only the one who controls himself when he is angry. A moment of patience in a moment of anger saves you a hundred moments of regret.

questions.question: Who is considered the strong man in the passage?
questions.explanation: True strength is defined by emotional control, not physical power.

title: The Morning Blessing
body: O Allah, by You we enter the morning and by You we enter the evening, by You we live and by You we die. Waking up is a blessing that many were not granted. Make your morning count.

questions.question: Waking up in the morning is described as what?
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that waking up is a blessing denied to many.

title: Sadaqah (Charity) Every Day
body: Every day the sun rises, charity is due on every joint of a person. A kind word is charity, removing a thorn from the path is charity, and smiling at your brother is charity.

questions.question: Which of these is considered charity (Sadaqah)?
questions.explanation: Even a smile is counted as a form of charity in Islam.

title: Trust in Allah
body: Tie your camel, then put your trust in Allah. Islam does not teach passivity. It teaches you to put in your maximum effort and then leave the result to the Almighty.

questions.question: What does 'Tie your camel' mean?
options: Take action first, then trust Allah
questions.explanation: It means to take practical steps and then rely on Allah.

title: Silence is Wisdom
body: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent. Words are like arrows; once released, they cannot be taken back.

questions.question: What should you do if you cannot speak good?
questions.explanation: The instruction is clear: speak good or stay silent.

title: Forgiveness
body: The one who does not show mercy to others will not be shown mercy. Forgiving others is not a sign of weakness; it is the ultimate sign of a strong and beautiful soul.

questions.question: Forgiving others is a sign of what?
questions.explanation: The passage states forgiveness is the ultimate sign of strength.

title: The Intention
body: Actions are judged by intentions. If you sleep with the intention to wake up and seek knowledge, even your sleep becomes an act of worship.

questions.question: Actions are judged by what?
questions.explanation: Intention is the foundation of every act in Islam.
